e.title: **把十九世纪的保险地图接回现代坐标**：一个工具用**街道标签的 OCR** 自动给**桑伯恩火灾保险地图**做地理配准，**输出 IIIF 地理配准标注**；**它的评测指标是**距离****——**逐字给出每册的「**≤25 英尺**」与「**≥200 英尺**」占比**（**如 97.6%／0.0%**）；**并逐字说明为什么用 **RANSAC** 而不是最小二乘**：「**我们对自家控制点的信心**远低于对人的」**，**且**「**把正确与错误的控制点平均起来**不太可能得到好模型**」
e.title_en: Reconnecting nineteenth-century insurance maps to modern coordinates: a tool uses optical character recognition of street labels to georeference Sanborn fire insurance maps automatically and emits a IIIF georeference annotation, with its evaluation measured in distance, giving for each volume the share of pages placed within twenty-five feet and the share beyond two hundred, and stating why it uses RANSAC rather than least squares because its confidence in its own ground control points is far lower than in a human one, so averaging a mix of correct and incorrect points is unlikely to produce a good model
e.title_hk: **把十九世紀的保險地圖接回現代坐標**：一個工具用**街道標籤的 OCR** 自動給**桑伯恩火災保險地圖**做地理配準，**輸出 IIIF 地理配準標註**；**它的評測指標是**距離****——**逐字給出每冊的「**≤25 英尺**」與「**≥200 英尺**」佔比**（**如 97.6%／0.0%**）；**並逐字說明為什麼用 **RANSAC** 而不是最小二乘**：「**我們對自家控制點的**信心遠低於對人的」**，**且**「**把正確與錯誤的控制點平均起來不太可能得到好模型**」
e.summary: 一个**自动给桑伯恩保险地图做地理配准的工具**（**★10**、**Apache-2.0**、Python、仓库体量 **160 MB**、**最后推送落在窗口之内**）：**逐字自述其目标为**「**自动给桑伯恩保险地图做地理配准**」**；**其最值得记的一处是它**用距离而不是比例来评测****——**逐字给出逐册结果表**，**含「**已放置页数**」（**如 27/33＝82%、103/109＝94%、124/129＝96%**）、**「**≤25 英尺**」占比**、**「**≥200 英尺**」占比**与**总分**（**如 97.6%／0.0%**）；**第二处是它**把方法选择讲成一段推理**——**逐字说明为什么用 **RANSAC** 而不是最小二乘**：**「**我们**对自家控制点的信心远低于对人的**」**；**「**把正确与错误的控制点平均起来不太可能得到好模型。**而**用 RANSAC 这种对离群点极其稳健的方法，**我们可以从噪声中找出哪怕一点点信号**」**；**第三处是它**把失败情形点名****（**逐字：**某区在 1911 年系统性改名了所有街道，**故**它在 1945 年的图上表现良好、**在 1898 年的图上表现很差****；**并逐字说**某个城市是「**噩梦场景**」**）
e.summary_hk: 一個**自動給桑伯恩保險地圖做地理配準的工具**（**★10**、**Apache-2.0**、Python、體量 **160 MB**、**最後推送落在窗口之內**）：**逐字自述其目標為**「**自動給桑伯恩保險地圖做地理配準**」**；**其最值得記的一處是它**用距離而不是比例來評測****——**逐字給出逐冊結果表**，**含「**已放置頁數**」（**如 27/33＝82%、103/109＝94%、124/129＝96%**）、**「**≤25 英尺**」佔比**、**「**≥200 英尺**」佔比**與**總分**（**如 97.6%／0.0%**）；**第二處是它**把方法選擇講成一段推理**——**逐字說明為什麼用 RANSAC 而不是最小二乘**：**「**我們對自家控制點的**信心遠低於對人的**」**；**「**把正確與錯誤的控制點平均起來不太可能得到好模型。**而**用 RANSAC 這種對離群點極其穩健的方法，**我們可以從噪聲中找出哪怕一點點信號**」**；**第三處是它**把失敗情形點名****（**某區在 1911 年系統性改名了所有街道，**故**它在 1945 年的圖上表現良好、**在 1898 年的圖上表現很差****；**並逐字說**某城市是「**噩夢場景**」**）
e.summary_en: A tool that georeferences Sanborn insurance maps automatically — 10 stars, Apache-2.0, Python, a 160 MB repository, last pushed inside the window — describing its goal verbatim as automatically georeferencing Sanborn insurance maps. **Its most notable feature is that it evaluates by distance rather than proportion**: a per-volume results table gives pages placed, the share within twenty-five feet and the share beyond two hundred feet, together with a score, for example 82 percent of pages placed and 97.6 percent within twenty-five feet with none beyond two hundred. **The second is that it presents its method choice as an argument**, stating verbatim why it uses RANSAC rather than least squares: its confidence in its own ground control points is far lower than in a human one, so averaging a mix of correct and incorrect points is unlikely to produce a good model, whereas a method extremely robust to outliers can find a little signal through the noise. **The third is that it names the cases where it fails**, verbatim that a borough which systematically renamed all its streets in 1911 is handled well on 1945 maps and terribly on 1898 maps, and that one city is described verbatim as a nightmare scenario.
e.body:
**mapsnap-georeferencer**（仓库 `danvk/mapsnap`）**是一个自动给桑伯恩保险地图做地理配准的工具**：**逐字自述为**「**The goal of Mapsnap is to automatically georeference Sanborn Insurance Maps.**」**。**实测 **★10**（**为本轮四条中关注度最高的一条**）、fork 0、许可 **Apache-2.0**（**实测仓库内含 `LICENSE` 文件，**raw 探测 HTTP 200**；**GitHub 许可字段亦为 Apache-2.0**）、主语言 Python、仓库体量 **160,321 KB**、**创建 2026-05-14**、最后推送 **2026-09-11**、默认分支 `main`**（**均 GitHub API 实测值；**创建与推送**都在解冻窗口之内****）；**README 实测 **33,514 字节**；**仓库实测共 **387 个文件、30 个目录**（**经 GitHub API tree 接口实测，`truncated` 为 false；含 `mapsnap/` 150 项、`app/` 128 项、**`testdata/` 48 项、**`gallery/` 25 项、**`images/` 23 项、**`models/` 10 项、**`scripts/` 10 项、**`baselines/` 7 项、**.github/` 4 项、`docs/` 4 项**）**。本条目属于本轮主题**「接线：把它接到另一套东西上能用为止」**；**⭐⭐⭐ 它是本轮四条里**唯一一条**把「接过去的东西」**用距离来度量**的****。

可核实信息（**均 README 与 tree 实测**）：⭐⭐⭐ **① 它把地图**自动接到坐标上**，并说明接出来的是什么**——**逐字为**：**「**After a few minutes, depending on the number of images in the Sanborn volume, you will get a **IIIF Georeference AnnotationPage** that you can view on Allmaps」**⭐⭐⭐ **四处值得记**：**① ⭐⭐⭐ **产物是**一个标准化的标注页**（**逐字 `IIIF Georeference AnnotationPage`**）**——**⭐ 即**它不是一张截图，**而是**别的地图工具能读的东西**（**⭐ 这正是本轮主题：**接到**既有的查看器**上**）；**② ⭐⭐⭐ **它有**一条两行的最小用法****（**逐字给出 `uv tool install mapsnap-cli`、**建目录、**下载清单、**在 OSM 上找一个包含该地图区域的关系、**再 `mapsnap run-loc mymap r1234567`**）**——**⭐ 即**「接线」**被压到一条命令**；**③ ⭐⭐ **输入之一是一个开放地图上的**关系编号**（**⭐ 即**它借用**别人的边界数据**来确定大致范围**）；**④ ⭐⭐ **耗时被如实说成「几分钟，**取决于该册的图幅数」****（**⭐ 即**没有承诺速度**）。**② ⭐⭐⭐ **它用**距离**而不是「比例」来评测，且同时给出**两端的比例****——**逐字给出逐册表**：**已放置页数**（**27/33＝82%、**103/109＝94%、**124/129＝96%**）、**「**≤25 英尺**」占比**、**「**≥200 英尺**」占比**、**总分**与**一个可点的查看器链接**⭐⭐⭐ **四处值得记**：**① ⭐⭐⭐ **指标是**距离阈值下的占比**（**25 英尺与 200 英尺**）**——**⭐ 即**「配准得好不好」**被翻译成**可数的地理误差**；**② ⭐⭐⭐ **同时报告**错得很离谱的比例**（**≥200 英尺**）**——**⭐ 本词条认为这是**最值得抄的一处评测设计**：**只看「有多准」不够，**还要看「有多离谱」****；**③ ⭐⭐⭐ **测试数据来自**志愿者手工配准**（**逐字注明「测试数据来自某志愿者站点上由人工完成的地理编码」**）**——**⭐ 即**参照物是**人的结果**；**④ ⭐⭐ **每一册都留一个**可打开的链接****（**⭐ 即**读者可以自己看它配得对不对**）。**③ ⭐⭐⭐ **它把**方法选择**写成一段有来有回的推理，而不是一句「用了 RANSAC」**——**逐字要点**：**先说明**其他工具用**全部控制点**拟合并用最小二乘，**「**你提供的每一个控制点都会影响模型」**；**再说明**它自己**「**用每一对控制点拟合一个候选模型，**再看这个模型能多好地解释街道标签。**最好的一对控制点被选中，**其余被丢弃。**它们对拟合没有直接影响」**；**然后给出理由**（**逐字「**我们对自家控制点的信心远低于对人的**」**；**「**」**；「**把正确与错误的控制点平均起来不太可能得到好模型。**而**用 RANSAC 这种对离群点极其稳健的方法，**我们可以从噪声中找出哪怕一点点信号」**）**；**最后**逐条列出**它为什么会错**（**OCR 误读、**街道在到达交叉口前转弯使外推失效、**标签被误解为另一条街**）**⭐⭐⭐ **三处值得记**：**① ⭐⭐⭐ **「**我们对自家控制点的信心远低于对人的**」是本条**最诚实的一句****（**⭐ 即**它解释了**为什么不能借用人类的做法**）；**② ⭐⭐⭐ **细读后才会发现的方法差别**（**六参数仿射对四参数 Helmert、**全部控制点对每对控制点取最优**）**——**⭐ 且**它给出**量级证据**（**逐字说明在人类配准结果里**尺度各向异性**多小于 **3%**、**斜切**多小于 **3°**，**「**两者都足够接近零，**以至于不清楚它们是真实的还是配准不准确的产物」**，**故**去掉这两个参数**只需两个控制点而非三个**）**；**③ ⭐⭐ **失败机制被逐条列出并**归因到具体组件****（**⭐ 例如**短街名**（**如「AVENUE T」「K ST」「1ST ST」**）**之所以难，**逐字归因于**底层 OCR 库对长文本更好、**而单个字母（O／X／M／W）的方向是歧义的****）。**④ ⭐⭐⭐ **它把「这个模型是怎么做出来的」也写出来**——**逐字要点**：**最初想用某个大模型 API 直接找交叉口**，**「**它做得还行，**但慢（**每题约 3 分钟**）、**贵（**每张约 0.10 美元**）且并不总是准确。**它在非骨架图上表现不好，**而且**过程不透明，**所以很难改进」**；**随后**意识到自己其实是在**用眼睛追踪街道标签来评价它找到的交叉口**，**于是**改让 OCR 做这件事**；**再后来**发现**「**细化那一步并没有帮助**」**，**遂**收敛到现在的模型**⭐⭐⭐ **三处值得记**：**① ⭐⭐⭐ **它给出了**放弃一条路线的三个可数理由**（**慢、**贵、**不透明**）**——**⭐ 其中**「过程不透明，所以难以改进」**是一句很少见的工程判断**；**② ⭐⭐⭐ **它说明**为什么最终回到本地 OCR****（**⭐ 即**「评价方式」**决定了**实现方式**）；**③ ⭐⭐ **它如实记录了**一个被删掉的步骤**（**⭐ 即**「细化阶段被证明没有帮助」**也留在了文档里**）。**⑤ ⭐⭐ **其余可核实细节**：**① **它有一节**与前人工作的对照****（**逐字说明另一篇论文的做法与它**基本相反**：**先用自定模型检测交叉口、**再用另一套 OCR 读水平或垂直条带里的街名**；**并逐字指出该做法**「**本质上无法找到斜向街道」**；**随后给出一个数字对照**——**「**至少对新奥尔良 1951，**Mapsnap 在它配准的图幅上有 **76%** 落在 **15 英尺**以内，**而该论文是 **14%****，**并**逐字自加保留**：「**我不确定他们测的是哪些地图，**而且他们还有别的判据，**所以这可能不是一个公平的比较」**）**（**⭐ 本词条认为这条**自加保留**是本条**第二处最值得抄的地方**）；**② **它有一节**明确列出考虑过的替代方案**（**用罗盘玫瑰判北、**用比例尺判尺度**）**，**并说明各自为何不用**（**逐字「**罗盘并不一定那么准，**用街道更好」**）**；**③ **它有一个**只有三个问题的问答节****（**逐字含「**这能用于其他类型的地图吗？**」「**它和某个志愿者站点是什么关系？**」「**它用 AI 吗？**」**）**——**⭐ 即**它预判了**读者最可能问的三件事**；**④ **它把**开发所借助的工具**也如实写出来**（**逐字说明两个 AI 编程工具**在让它跑起来这件事上**都起了关键作用**）**。**⑥ ⭐⭐ 可与本站条目并读**：[[oldinsurancemaps]]、[[asgs]]、[[pyincore]]、[[duckdb-fema-nfip]]、[[openquake-engine]]。

⚠️ **如实标注**：**① ⭐ **许可为 **Apache-2.0****（**实测仓库内含 `LICENSE`，**raw 探测 HTTP 200**，**GitHub 字段亦为 Apache-2.0**）**——**⭐ 而**本词条**未读该文件内容**，**⚠️ 亦**未核实其**测试数据与图幅影像**的权利（**⭐ 其中含来自公共机构的扫描地图**——**这是「代码许可」与「其中的资料权利」两件事**）。**② ⚠️⚠️⚠️ **本次**没有运行它的任何一步****——**未安装其命令行工具、未下载任何清单或影像、未运行 `mapsnap`、未打开其任何查看器链接、未打开任何图**；**故**本词条**不主张**其地理配准、其评测数字或其 IIIF 产物**按其所述工作**——**⭐ 本词条核实到的是**README 的**逐字内容**（**含其性能表、方法推理、失败情形与开发经过**）与**其经 tree 接口实测的目录结构**。**③ ⚠️⚠️ **未读其任何源码或 `docs/` 下的文档****（**⭐ 即**未核对**其地址解析率是否可达、**其 RANSAC 实现与阈值选取、**以及**其四参数模型是否如其所述**）**——**⭐ 这是本条目**最需要后续核实的一处**。**④ ⚠️ **未核实**其性能表的数字**（**⭐ 即**表中每一行的比例**本词条**均未复核**，**也未打开那些被标注为「查看」的链接**）。**⑤ ⭐ ⚠️ **不主张**其方法可用于任何特定城市或年代**（**⭐ 其自述已逐字给出失败情形**，**本词条只是转述**）。**⑥ ⚠️ **★10、fork 0**，**且**未核实作者背景**。**⑦ ⚠️ **创建与推送均在解冻窗口之内（2026-05-14／2026-09-11）****。**⑧ ⚠️ **本条目所记为**2026-09-11 所见****。**核实说明**：`https://api.github.com/repos/danvk/mapsnap` 于 2026-09-11 经仓库检索接口与 GitHub API 实测读取（★数、许可 Apache-2.0、语言、体量、创建／推送时间、默认分支）；README **33,514 字节**经 `raw.githubusercontent.com` 实测逐字核对（**含其性能表、How it Works、Notes on the model、Prior Art 与 Questions 各节**）；`LICENSE` 的存在经 raw 探测确认（HTTP 200）；**文件清单经 GitHub API tree 接口实测（387 个文件、30 个目录，`truncated` 为 false）**；**未克隆、未安装任何依赖、未运行任何命令、未下载任何清单或影像、未打开任何查看器或图、未读任何源码或文档内容、未做其他网络观察**。

## 同类工具
[[naphia]]、[[npi]]、[[tenzi-broker-resources]]、[[aviareto]]、[[ecb-data]]

mymap r1234567`）；**③ ⭐⭐輸入之一是一個開放地圖上的關係編號**（借用別人的邊界數據定大致範圍）；**④ ⭐⭐耗時如實說成「幾分鐘，取決於該冊的圖幅數」**。**② ⭐⭐⭐ **用**距離**而不是比例來評測，且同時給出**兩端的比例****——逐字逐冊表：已放置頁數（27/33＝82%、103/109＝94%、124/129＝96%）、「≤25 英尺」佔比、「≥200 英尺」佔比、總分與可點的查看器鏈接**四處**：**① ⭐⭐⭐指標是距離閾值下的佔比**（25 英尺與 200 英尺——「配準得好不好」被翻譯成**可數的地理誤差**）；**② ⭐⭐⭐同時報告**錯得很離譜的比例**（≥200 英尺——只看「有多準」不夠，還要看「有多離譜」，**最值得抄的一處評測設計**）；**③ ⭐⭐⭐測試數據來自志願者手工配準**（參照物是**人的結果**）；**④ ⭐⭐每一冊都留一個可打開的鏈接**。**③ ⭐⭐⭐ **把方法選擇寫成一段有來有回的推理**——逐字要點：其他工具用**全部控制點**＋最小二乘（「你提供的每一個控制點都會影響模型」）；它自己**用每一對控制點擬合一個候選模型**、**最好的一對被選中、其餘被丟棄**（「它們對擬合沒有直接影響」）；理由是「**我們對自家控制點的**信心遠低於對人的**」**；**「**把正確與錯誤的控制點平均起來不太可能得到好模型。而用 RANSAC 這種對離群點極其穩健的方法，我們可以從噪聲中找出哪怕一點點信號」；最後逐條列出它為什麼會錯（OCR 誤讀／街道在到達交叉口前轉彎使外推失效／標籤被誤解為另一條街）**三處**：**① ⭐⭐⭐「我們對自家控制點的信心遠低於對人的」是本條最誠實的一句**；**② ⭐⭐⭐細讀後才會發現的方法差別**（六參數仿射對四參數 e.body_en:
**mapsnap-georeferencer** (repository `danvk/mapsnap`) **is a tool that georeferences Sanborn insurance maps automatically**, stating its goal verbatim as automatically georeferencing Sanborn insurance maps. **Measured 10 stars, the highest-attention entry of this round, 0 forks, licence Apache-2.0 with a licence file measurably present and answering 200 to a raw probe and the GitHub field agreeing, primary language Python, a 160,321 KB repository, created 2026-05-14, last pushed 2026-09-11, default branch main** (all GitHub API measurements; ⭐ **creation and push both inside the thaw window**); **the README measures 33,514 bytes**; **the repository measures 387 files and 30 directories**, read through the trees endpoint with truncation false, holding a package directory, an application directory, test data, a gallery, images, models, scripts, baselines and small documentation and workflow directories. This entry belongs to this round’s theme of **wiring something up so that another system can use it**, and ⭐⭐⭐ **of the four it is the only one that measures the connection in distance**.

Verifiable details (**read from the README and measured in the tree**): ⭐⭐⭐ **① It connects the maps to coordinates automatically and says what comes out** — verbatim, after a few minutes depending on the number of images in the volume, **you get a IIIF Georeference AnnotationPage that you can view on Allmaps** ⭐⭐⭐ **Four things**: ⭐⭐⭐ **the product is a standardised annotation page rather than a picture, so other map tools can read it**, ⭐ **which is exactly this round’s theme of connecting to an existing viewer**; ⭐⭐⭐ **a minimal two-line usage is given**, installing a command-line tool, creating a directory, downloading a manifest, finding an open-map relation containing the map area and running one command, ⭐ **so the wiring is compressed into one command**; ⭐⭐ **one input is a relation identifier on an open map, so it borrows someone else’s boundary data to establish the rough extent**; **and ⭐⭐ the running time is stated honestly as minutes depending on the volume’s page count**, ⭐ **with no speed promised**. **② ⭐⭐⭐ It evaluates by distance rather than proportion and reports both ends** — a per-volume table gives pages placed at 27 of 33, 103 of 109 and 124 of 129, **the share within twenty-five feet and the share beyond two hundred feet**, a score and a clickable viewer link ⭐⭐⭐ **Four things**: ⭐⭐⭐ **the metric is a share under a distance threshold, so how well the georeferencing went is translated into a countable geographic error**; ⭐⭐⭐ **it also reports how badly wrong the failures are**, ⭐ **which this entry considers the most copyable evaluation design here, since knowing how accurate it is, is not enough without knowing how wrong it can be**; ⭐⭐⭐ **the test data come from hand geocoding by volunteers, so the reference is a human result**; **and ⭐⭐ every volume carries a link a reader can open to judge for themselves**. **③ ⭐⭐⭐ It presents its method choice as an argument with both sides** — verbatim, other tools fit using all control points and least squares, **so every point you provide influences the model**, whereas this tool **fits a candidate model from each pair of points, chooses the best pair and discards the rest, which then have no direct influence on the fit**, **the stated reason being that confidence in its own control points is far lower than in a human’s, so averaging a mix of correct and incorrect points is unlikely to produce a good model, while a method extremely robust to outliers can find a little signal through the noise**, followed by an itemised list of why it errs, from misread text through a street turning before an intersection to a label being taken for a different street ⭐⭐⭐ **Three things**: ⭐⭐⭐ **the sentence about confidence in its own control points being lower than in a human’s is the most honest line here**, ⭐ **since it explains why the human practice cannot be borrowed**; ⭐⭐⭐ **the method difference is only visible on close reading, a six-parameter affine model against a four-parameter one, all control points against the best pair**, **and it supplies magnitude evidence verbatim**, human georeferencing showing scale anisotropy mostly under three percent and skew mostly under three degrees, **both close enough to zero that it is unclear whether they are real or artefacts of inaccurate georeferencing**, so dropping them needs two control points rather than three; **and ⭐⭐ failure mechanisms are itemised and attributed to specific components**, short street names being hard verbatim because the underlying recogniser works better with longer runs of text and **the orientation of a single letter is ambiguous**. **④ ⭐⭐⭐ It also writes how the model was developed** — verbatim, the initial idea was to ask a large-model interface to find intersections, which **did an acceptable job but was slow at about three minutes per task, expensive at about ten cents per image and not always accurate**, doing poorly on maps that are not skeletons, **and whose process was opaque, making it hard to improve on**, after which the author realised he was evaluating its intersections by mentally tracing street labels, so the labels were handed to optical recognition instead, and later that **the refinement step was not helping**, leaving the present model ⭐⭐⭐ **Three things**: ⭐⭐⭐ **three countable reasons are given for abandoning a route, slow, expensive and opaque**, ⭐ **of which opaque and therefore hard to improve on is a rare piece of engineering judgement**; ⭐⭐⭐ **it says why it ended up with local recognition, so how it was evaluated determined how it was implemented**; **and ⭐⭐ a deleted step is recorded rather than hidden**. **⑤ ⭐⭐ Other details**: **a prior-art section contrasts an earlier paper’s essentially reversed approach**, detecting intersections with a custom model and then reading street labels in horizontal or vertical strips, **which it notes inherently cannot find diagonal streets**, and gives a numeric comparison — **at least for one 1951 volume, this tool places 76 percent of the images it maps within fifteen feet against 14 percent for that paper** — ⚠️ **with the repository adding the caveat verbatim that it is unsure which maps they tested on and that they have other criteria, so it may not be a fair comparison**, ⭐ **which this entry takes as the second most copyable item here**; **a section lists alternatives considered**, such as a compass rose or a scale bar, **with the reasons each was not used**; **a three-question section anticipates what readers most likely ask**, including whether it works on other map types and whether it uses artificial intelligence; **and the artificial-intelligence coding tools used in building it are stated**. **⑥ ⭐⭐ Readable with** [[oldinsurancemaps]], [[asgs]], [[pyincore]], [[duckdb-fema-nfip]] and [[openquake-engine]].

⚠️ **Stated plainly**: **① ⭐ The licence is Apache-2.0** — **a licence file is measurably present, answering 200 to a raw probe, and the GitHub field agrees**, ⚠️ **with its contents and the rights in its test data and map imagery not verified**, ⭐ **those including scans from public institutions, so rights in the code and rights in the material are two different things**. **② ⚠️⚠️⚠️ Nothing in it was run** — **the command-line tool was not installed, no manifest or imagery was downloaded, the tool was not run, no viewer link was opened and no image was opened**; **so this entry does not claim its georeferencing, its evaluation figures or its annotation output works as described**, ⭐ **what it verified being the verbatim README, including its performance table, its method argument, its failure cases and its development history, and the directory structure measured through the trees endpoint**. **③ ⚠️⚠️ Neither its source nor the documentation under its docs directory was read**, ⭐ **so whether the placement rates are attainable, how the robust fitting and its thresholds are implemented, and whether the four-parameter model is as described were not checked** — ⭐ **the single most important thing to verify next for this entry**. **④ ⚠️ The figures in its performance table were not verified**, ⭐ **no row re-checked and none of the viewer links opened**. **⑤ ⭐ ⚠️ No claim is made that the method works for any particular city or era**, ⭐ **its own failure cases being reported here rather than endorsed**. **⑥ ⚠️ At 10 stars with no forks the author’s background was not verified**. **⑦ ⚠️ Creation and push both fall inside the thaw window**. **⑧ ⚠️ This entry records what was seen on 2026-09-11**. **Verification note**: the repository was read on 2026-09-11 through the repository search endpoint and the GitHub API for stars, licence, language, size, dates and default branch; the 33,514-byte readme was read via `raw.githubusercontent.com` and checked verbatim, **including its performance table, its how-it-works section, its model notes, its prior-art section and its questions**; a licence probe against the root returned 200; **the file listing was read through the trees endpoint, 387 files and 30 directories with truncation false**; **nothing was cloned, no dependency was installed, no command was run, no manifest or imagery was downloaded, no viewer or image was opened, no source or documentation content was read, and no other network observation was made**.
